A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OmniSAM research and contain readable main text, equations, Tables 1–10, Figures 1–10, and complete supplementary material. The additional page in v3 reflects reflow.

before.justification: V2 reports original segmentation experiments across three adaptation scenarios, with quantitative results, ablations, and qualitative analyses in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: V3 retains the original segmentation results, ablations, and qualitative analyses reported in v2.

M1.justification: The SAM2/LoRA architecture, patch sequencing, memory mechanism, semantic decoder, dynamic pseudo-label updating, and FoV-based prototypical adaptation remain unchanged in Section 3 and the supplement.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five datasets and three scenarios: SPin8-to-SPan8, CS13-to-DP13, and SP13-to-DP13. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding tables, including 360SFUDA++ in Table 2, DATR-S and DTA4PASS in Table 3, and the source-only and adaptation comparators in Table 4.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and supplementary Section 1 retain the stated splits, class subsets, preprocessing, optimizer settings, model variants, nine-frame processing, and sampling of 400 target images per epoch.

E4.justification: The loss and pseudo-label ablations, memory-bank-size study, lambda sensitivity analysis, memory-mechanism comparisons, segmentation examples, and t-SNE analysis are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All tabulated values and plotted or qualitative results match. Tables 2–4 retain the headline mIoUs of 79.06, 62.46, and 54.61 for the same models and scenarios; supplementary results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The shared-distortion assumption, prototype definitions and update rule, and equations (1)–(8) are unchanged. No formal results, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, methodological contributions, and performance claims. The new code-availability statement does not alter the scientific claims.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations concerning indoor annotation quality and limited indoor prototypical-adaptation benefits, the model-size/inference-speed tradeoff, and the limitation concerning Syn2Real performance.

D1.justification: V3 adds a source-code availability statement and a link to the Ding-Zhong/OmniSAM repository in the abstract; v2 provides no such link. Other implementation and reproducibility details are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 46 references and research-positioning passages are retained. Changed citation back-reference page numbers result from pagination.

P1.justification: V3 appends a brief code-availability statement to the abstract and updates the version/date stamp. The remaining prose and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure content and table structures are unchanged, but placement and pagination shift. Figure 4 moves within page 7, Figure 5 moves to page 8, and the limitations paragraph spills onto a nearly empty page 9.

improvement.justification: The added source-code statement and repository pointer provide a modest improvement in reproducibility guidance. Scientific content is unchanged, and the awkward limitations-page break is a small presentation drawback. The PDFs establish the added access information, but cannot establish the repository's completeness or usability.
